text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000110 bills 99215 far above the risk-adjusted expectation on a heavily multi-morbid panel, but the small sample of returned charts mostly supports the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely complex: most visits are on patients with 5+ conditions, and almost no 99215s fall on 0–1 condition patients (sampled exceptions include C0057861 and C0058186). However, the expected share already adjusts for complexity, and within every complexity stratum this provider's 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider share, so sicker patients alone do not obviously explain the excess. Against that, the documented 99215s are unsupported at close to the peer rate, and supported examples such as C0058383 and C0058412 show high MDM with plausible minutes. Those charts cover only about 4% of claims, though, and there are softer signs the notes may be inflated or templated: some notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim, time entries repeat in about 16% of notes, and no audit trail was received. A reviewer should first request a larger stratified chart sample focused on 5+ condition 99215 visits, plus the EHR audit trail. They should check whether the documented MDM and data elements reflect actual work, starting with data-flagged notes like C0057752 and C0058040 and repeated-time entries."}
